gaps.evading_example: The cubic-aliasing caveat on the derivative skewness is priced for the 2/3 band only, while two wider bands are offered as first-class options and the skewness gates the default warm-up. `derivative_skewness` (src/Observables.jl): "Because ⟨det S⟩ is a **cubic** invariant, its grid mean carries a small residual aliasing on a ``2/3``-truncated field — negligible for a well-resolved run, but, unlike the quadratic reductions, not exactly alias-free." `Simulation` offers "`dealiasing = TwoThirds()` — the DealiasingStrategy (2/3 sharp, `HouLi` smooth, or `PhaseShift`)", and `kinetic_energy` states the retained bands: "`HouLi` keeps the full band κ_max = N/2" and PhaseShift's "wider √2N/3 band". Cubic aliasing on an N³ grid requires 3κ_max ≥ N: at 2/3 that is 3κ_max = N exactly, so only corner triads fold — the "small residual" is true. At PhaseShift's √2N/3 it is 3κ_max ≈ 1.41N and at HouLi's N/2 it is 1.5N, a genuine band of folding triads, and PhaseShift's half-cell shift-average provably cancels only QUADRATIC odd-axis aliases, so it buys the cubic nothing. `derivative_skewness` is the strict gate of `StationarityCriterion` (`gate_skewness = true`, `skew_floor = 0.1`), so under `dealiasing = HouLi()` the automatic "is this developed turbulence yet" decision is taken on a number whose contamination no document bounds. Crucially this is NOT a fossil: `git log -S` puts PhaseShift at 18b84cd (199 commits back) and the 2/3-scoped caveat at a9dd51d (187 back) — the caveat was authored under-scoped with all three strategies already shipped, and both lie far outside hat 22's prescribed `git log --oneline -40` window.

gaps.gap: THE STATUS QUO IS MADE NORMATIVE, AND NOTHING EXTERNAL ADJUDICATES. Two lanes are instructed to derive the standard from the corpus: hat 16 — "derive the norm from the corpus itself (majority style), not an external guide"; hat 11 — "infer the implicit template the corpus follows and STATE it. THEN flag every OUTLIER". This inverts the project's own rule that legacy is not evidence of correctness. Two failure directions follow, and both are live. FALSE NEGATIVE: a convention that is uniformly wrong is invisible, because the instrument's evidence of wrongness IS divergence. FALSE POSITIVE, the worse one: where the majority is wrong and one instance is right, the correct instance is reported as the defect and the prescribed repair degrades the corpus. And because the corpus's majority was itself written by three prior rounds of this same panel, the baseline is the instrument's own output — the fixed point of the procedure is uniformity, not truth. No lane holds package TERMINOLOGY against anything external: hat 5 checks "physical definitions, conservation laws, scaling laws, dimensionless constants" (a name is none of these), hat 15 checks citation consistency and overclaims, hat 3 checks the code name across pages.

gaps.gap: THE PANEL HAS NO DENOMINATOR, SO ITS OUTPUT IS EVIDENCE OF YIELD AND IS USED AS EVIDENCE OF COVERAGE. Nothing in the design measures recall. There is no held-out set, no seeded-defect calibration, no lane that reports what it examined rather than what it found. Three mechanisms in the design actively erase the denominator: (i) run order is priority order and "a token-out truncates the tail", so a run's output is a function of budget with nothing normalizing for it; (ii) several personas forbid reporting unexamined material (hat 8: "Report ONLY quantified claims you actually checked member-by-member"), so a hat that checked three claims and a hat that checked three hundred are indistinguishable in the output; (iii) the sole recall instrument is a trip-wire at N = 0 ("a hat returning zero findings is flagged"), useless at N = 3. Compounding it, the design counts AGREEMENT as corroboration — hat 1: "if you and another hat both find it, that agreement is useful evidence" — but the hats are draws from one model with one training and one set of dispositions, so agreement is the same reading taken twice, not independent confirmation. Consequently the panel's output supports only an existential claim (at least these defects exist) and is consumed as a universal one (the docs are sound). And there is no route by which anyone would learn it had missed something: the only oracle the project actually has is the user's eye, which sits outside the instrument, and the instrument's whole growth history is that it acquires a lane only AFTER some other means has already found the class — which guarantees it lags its own oracle permanently.

gaps.gap: A COMPOSED IDENTITY THAT NO SINGLE PAGE STATES AND NO LANE TESTS. The consistency-matrix hat — the panel's declared spine — builds a matrix of each recurring ENTITY and diffs the versions of THAT entity across pages. It never composes two DIFFERENT entities' statements into a derived identity and tests whether the code satisfies it. Composing the two: the denominator is k. The code (`src/Observables.jl`) computes `total = sum(broadcast((k, e) -> k > 0 ? e : zero(e), κ, E))` — the κ = 0 shell EXCLUDED — so the denominator is k − E₀, not k. The exclusion, and its reason, exist only in a `#` comment: "Testing `sum(E)` instead let a field whose energy is entirely in the mean flow pass the emptiness guard and return a meaningless zero." Provenance: commit 1eef136 changed `total = sum(E)` to the κ>0 form, touched `src/Observables.jl`, `src/Particles.jl`, `src/SimulationRun.jl`, and no `docs/src/` page. HONEST BOUND ON THE HARM, since it is conditional: the package's own seeder zeroes the κ = 0 mode (`src/State.jl:117-123`) and the Leray-projected dynamics with shell-1–2 forcing preserve that, so for a front-door run E₀ = 0 and the two denominators coincide numerically. There L₁₁ is normalized against an energy that no other reported quantity uses, and the documented identity a physicist would validate against — Σ_n E_n = k — is silently not the one the code applies.

it also never learns that the function can throw `ArgumentError` on a zero-energy field, another absence with no text. 1/2 free readers: the passage reads as unusually rigorous — it volunteers the midpoint-quadrature caveat and the low-shell resolution limit — which reads as thoroughness and disarms suspicion. 4 architect, 7 existence-auditor: the public form and the set of forms are fine. 10 conceptual-clarity: physics category errors are explicitly the physics hats' property, and this one is a physics object. 11 structure, 16 style, 17 cold-reader, 18 plain-sense: shape, uniformity, self-containedness, and meaningfulness are all satisfied. 12 latex: the display block is idiomatic. 15 citations: classical, uncited by convention. 19 naming, 20 doc-policy: the docstring is policy-perfect — physical meaning first, formula in a display block, `# Fields` absent because it is a function. 21 invariants: no invariant or decision covers a summation range. 22 fossil-and-drift: commit 1eef136's message is "Round 5: seven fixed including a backwards-clock blocker" — it names no rename, no signature change, no retirement, no default change, so this lane's step (1) does not select it and its step (2) has no old identifier to grep. 23 pf-parity: PF owns `radial_spectrum`; gaps.proposed_lens: No lens — this needs a different mechanism. A reading hat cannot reliably form and test derived identities across docstrings; the check is executable. The package already owns the right instrument: `test/optimality_audit.jl` and `test/validation.jl` pin numerical relations. Add an IDENTITY test file that asserts each cross-docstring equation the corpus states — `sum(energy_spectrum(û,d).energy) ≈ kinetic_energy(û)`, `integral_scale`'s denominator against that same sum, `dissipation`'s two routes against each other on a solenoidal field — on a field deliberately carrying a nonzero mean mode, so the negative control is the case the docs' composition claims to cover. Then have the panel's doc-policy lane cite the identity file rather than re-derive it.

gaps.gap: The closure-audit stage that gives the panel its adversarial teeth is hardcoded to a hat roster that lags the panel's own persona list, so an entire generation of lanes runs collect-only forever with no independent check that any of their findings are real, fixed, or silently dropped.
gaps.evading_example: verify.js (.claude/commands/check-consistency/verify.js, lines 42-48) defines `const ALL_HATS = [...]` with exactly 15 entries ending at '15-invariants-and-decisions'. panel.js (same directory) currently defines 23 hats (`grep -c "key: '"` = 23), including free-reader-a, free-reader-b, existence-auditor, quantifier-auditor, fossil-and-drift, pf-parity, logician, and conceptual-clarity -- precisely the eight newest lanes this whole review is asked to distrust most. `git log` shows verify.js was last touched at commit 406c333 ('Adversarially audit the instruments'), and panel.js was extended TWICE afterward with no matching verify.js commit (5297e66 '15 hats -> 21', e35a3af 'add a logician'). The live pile on disk confirms it is not hypothetical: `.claude/doc-review/` and its `closure/` subdirectory each hold exactly 15 files, 01 through 15 -- the eight newest hats have never once been run through this instrument's own closure loop in this repo's history. A default `verify.js` invocation (no `hats` filter, the documented usage) silently verifies only the 15 it knows, logs `complete: true` and a clean anomaly list, and never mentions the other eight exist. A real, harmful defect banked by `logician` or `pf-parity` -- say a genuinely false claim about the integrating-factor's floating-point stability, or a citation PF's own rulebook would flag as wrong -- can be reported, ranked in the summary, allegedly fixed, and NEVER independently re-checked, forever, while every dashboard the tooling prints reads clean.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: panel.js: not this stage's job -- it banks fine, the defect is downstream. 00-SUMMARY consolidation (an agent's free read of the NN-*.md files): it only sees what got banked; nothing tells it verify.js's roster is short. verify.js itself: actively produces a false all-clear -- its own `anomalies` array and `complete` flag are computed only over the 15 hats it iterates, so 'complete: true' is true-for-a-strict-subset while reading as true-for-the-panel. The `hats` selector guard (which throws on an unmatched name) only protects an EXPLICIT filter argument; the default, undirected run never exercises that guard at all. coverage.py is the one stage that WOULD catch it -- it globs `pile/[0-9][0-9]-*.md` directly rather than trusting a hardcoded list, so hats 16-23 would show as 'NO VERDICT FILE' -- but it is a separate, manually-invoked script the command file calls mandatory in prose only; nothing forces it to run, nothing greps its exit code automatically, and an operator satisfied by verify.js's own 'complete: true' has no structural prompt to run the one check that would contradict it.
gaps.proposed_lens: Kill the duplicate roster outright: have panel.js emit a manifest (`pile/hats.json`, the literal `.key` list it just ran) as part of its own output, and make verify.js read that manifest instead of hardcoding ALL_HATS -- staleness becomes structurally impossible rather than a maintained-by-hand comment (the comment 'KEEP THIS LIST IN STEP WITH panel.js' has now failed silently three times: 8->11->15->21->23, each growth outrunning the copy). Failing that minimally: make verify.js's own reported `complete` false whenever `pile`'s hat-file glob count differs from `ALL_HATS.length`, so the discrepancy surfaces inside the tool everyone already reads instead of only inside the tool nobody is forced to run.

gaps.gap: Severity and confidence are asserted exactly once, by the same interested agent that produced the finding, are explicitly shielded from override at the one human-facing stage ('a severity in the summary never overrides the hat's own'), and are dropped from the schema entirely at the one stage built to adversarially re-check claims -- so a magnitude error (a real defect correctly reported but wrongly rated) has no detector anywhere in the pipeline, unlike every other failure mode this design names and guards (dead agent, empty tally, stale roster, false ABSENT).
gaps.evading_example: panel.js's SCHEMA (lines 50-65) requires `severity: enum[blocker,major,minor,nit]` and `confidence: enum[high,medium,low]` per finding, self-chosen by the hat. verify.js's SCHEMA (lines 74-92) carries only `finding, title, verdict, evidence, surviving_class` -- no severity field exists to re-derive or contest. Concretely: suppose the economy-model `dns-practitioner` hat (18 of 23 hats run on the cheap Sonnet scan per the cost-mode design) finds a genuine hidden host-device sync inserted into the hot loop -- a blocker under the package's own GPU-primary invariant (CLAUDE.md invariant 4) and exactly the class of bug the project has fixed before (memory: 'optimality-audit-decision-35' lists such fixes). If the hat, under the pressure of ranking against 24 other candidates for its 25-item cap, labels it 'minor' -- whether from a scan-model's shallower read or simple miscalibration -- it survives every mechanical safeguard in this design: it is not a dead agent, not an empty tally, not a stale hat (assume it's one of the 15 verify.js still checks), and verify.js's PRESENT-default will faithfully confirm the bug is STILL THERE at every future round -- correctly reported, permanently mis-triaged, because the one field that would let a downstream reader deprioritize correctly is asserted once and never rechecked.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: The hat itself has no external calibration signal -- it is graded against nothing. 00-SUMMARY consolidation is explicitly instructed not to override the hat's self-assigned severity ('re-read the hat before downgrading anything'), which forecloses the one place a human eye could catch a mislabel. verify.js cannot catch it because its schema has no severity field to carry forward or contest -- a PARTIAL/PRESENT verdict says the defect is real but says nothing about whether 'minor' was ever the right word. coverage.py only counts verdicts against banked findings by number; it has no concept of severity at all. rubric_audit.js tests whether a hat's PERSONA produces a given finding, not whether the SEVERITY it assigns is well-calibrated -- a different question entirely.
gaps.proposed_lens: Add a blind severity-recalibration pass, structurally identical to rubric_audit's blind-run design: sample N banked findings, strip the hat's self-assigned severity, show only the quoted passage and the defect description to a fresh agent, and have it independently assign severity; compare distributions. Systematic disagreement (not scatter, a directional skew) is the calibration signal no stage currently produces. Absent that, at minimum let verify.js's verdict schema carry a `severity_check` field so the adversarial stage that already exists is asked the magnitude question, not just the existence question.

gaps.gap: The per-hat 25-finding cap has no accompanying signal of how much was cut, so a hat that legitimately found far more defects than the cap silently discards the tail with zero trace -- one stage before the very rule ('the summary must not contain an unenumerated bucket') that was built to stop exactly this kind of silent loss, and therefore invisible to it.
gaps.evading_example: panel.js's preamble (line 80) instructs every hat: 'report at most your 25 MOST SIGNIFICANT findings... Be selective: 15 sharp findings beat 50 padded ones.' Nothing in the SCHEMA records a candidate count, a truncation flag, or even a rough 'N more below the cap' note -- contrast this with verify.js's own `findings_in_file` field, which exists specifically to cross-check that a verifier didn't silently under-report (line 78: 'how many findings the banked hat file contains... NOT how many you adjudicated'). That exact discipline is absent one phase earlier, in the phase that actually produces the findings. `consistency-matrix` is told outright to be 'the spine' and 'build a MATRIX of every recurring entity... across ALL pages' -- on a 23-page corpus with the renaming history `fossil-and-drift`'s own premise documents (repeated field/symbol renames -- trajectory_sample -> particle_velocities, derived -> cache, and others per the repo's own commit log), it is entirely plausible this hat's honest tally of genuine cross-page divergences exceeds 25. If it does, the 00-SUMMARY anti-bucket rule (explicitly built to stop a ranking from silently becoming a scoping decision) cannot rescue what never reached a banked file in the first place -- it operates only on findings that survived into `NN-*.md`.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: The hat itself has every incentive to look thorough (it self-reports 'up to 25, ranked') and no incentive or mechanism to report what it dropped -- the persona rewards apparent selectivity, not honesty about recall. 00-SUMMARY consolidation reads only the banked files; a truncated hat and a genuinely-exhaustive-at-11-findings hat are indistinguishable to it. verify.js only adjudicates what's IN the banked file (`findings_in_file` counts THAT file's contents) -- it has no way to ask whether the file itself is a truncated view of a larger true set. coverage.py counts banked findings vs. verdicts, which is silent on whether banked-findings-count reflects true-defect-count.
gaps.proposed_lens: Extend the panel SCHEMA with a required `candidates_considered: integer` (or `truncated: boolean`) field, mirroring the `findings_in_file` self-report already used downstream in verify.js -- so a hat that hit the ceiling says so, and the 00-SUMMARY anti-bucket discipline has something to enumerate against instead of a hard floor it cannot see past.

gaps.gap: The summary's stated ranking heuristic ('severity x corroboration -- a defect found by many hats is a strong signal') structurally discounts source-grounded defects, because only a small minority of the 23 lanes ever read `src/*.jl`, so a real code-vs-docs drift defect has a hard corroboration ceiling far below a purely cosmetic rendered-prose issue that all 23 lanes can equally notice.
gaps.evading_example: Of the 23 hats, only naming-policy, doc-policy, invariants-and-decisions, latex-typesetter, and fossil-and-drift (via git grep/show) ever read this package's own `src/*.jl`; `software-architect`'s own persona says outright 'a separate code-level pass would read the source' -- i.e. it deliberately does not. So a defect only visible by diffing a docstring's claim against the actual implementation (a stale default value, a formula that drifted from a since-changed normalization constant -- the kind of thing this project has hit before, per memory's 'Yaglom 4/3 factor-2 BLOCKER') can be corroborated by at most ~5 of 23 hats even at unanimous agreement among everyone equipped to see it, while a citation-format inconsistency or an awkward sentence is visible to and correlated across all 23 rendered-text readers. Under 'severity x corroboration', a trivial but universally-visible style nit can structurally outrank a severe, code-verified physics error simply because more lenses happen to share the same vantage point on it.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: This is a property of the RANKING FORMULA itself, applied uniformly at the 00-SUMMARY stage -- no individual hat is positioned to notice it, because no hat sees the corroboration count across the whole panel; only the human-facing consolidation step computes it, and that step's brief ('rank by severity x corroboration') never asks whether the exposure to each defect class is symmetric across lanes before treating agreement as a validity signal.
gaps.proposed_lens: Weight corroboration by the substrate-exposure denominator, not the raw panel size -- e.g. report corroboration as 'k of n hats that could plausibly see this class' (rendered-only vs. source-reading), so a 4-of-5 source-verified defect is legible as strong evidence rather than diluted against a 19-of-23 prose nit. No existing lane supplies this; it is a fix to the consolidation heuristic, not a new lens.

gaps.gap: The panel's false-negative rate is fundamentally unmeasured on any recurring basis: the one instrument built to estimate rubric recall is bounded to a frozen, historical set of already-human-discovered defects, was run once, and is not wired into the documented, mandatory workflow -- so it cannot speak to defects nobody has ever found, which is the actual quantity a false-negative rate needs.
gaps.evading_example: rubric_audit.js exists and is genuinely well-built (blind persona re-runs, disjoint substrate/defect files, default-to-MISSED scoring) -- but its own header names its ground truth as 'the user's task of 2026-08-17', and rubric_prep.py draws `findings.json` from that one fixed pile. It answers 'would hat X's persona, run blind, have caught a defect a human already found on that date?' -- not 'how many real defects in the CURRENT corpus does the CURRENT 23-hat, economy-model panel miss?' The command file that documents the panel's required workflow (check-consistency.md, steps 1-7: build, consolidate, archive, run, summarize, verify, coverage-gate) never mentions rubric_audit.js by name -- grepping it for 'rubric' returns only two incidental prose mentions, not a numbered step. So the single tool capable of estimating recall is orphaned from the routine cadence: it does not re-run per round, its index does not grow as new human reads surface new known-missed classes, and it was never designed to measure recall against genuinely unknown defects (which by definition it cannot, since its index is built from things a human already caught). The honest current answer to 'what is the panel's false-negative rate' is: nobody knows, and the one measurement that gets closest answers a narrower question and was taken once.
gaps.why_each_lane_misses: verify.js and coverage.py measure closure (did a banked finding get fixed), not discovery (what fraction of true defects got banked in the first place) -- a different axis entirely. rubric_audit.js measures discovery, but only against a convenience sample of previously-human-found defects, so its ceiling is exactly the recall of the human read-through it was built from, not the recall of the panel against ground truth. No stage anywhere plants a KNOWN defect with a KNOWN answer into the corpus before a round and checks recovery -- the only way to get a denominator that is not itself a product of somebody's prior attention.
gaps.proposed_lens: Seeded-defect (mutation-testing) injection, run every round rather than once: before each panel round, inject N deliberately fabricated, categorized, ground-truth-labeled defects into a disposable copy of the built docs (a wrong normalization constant, a broken cross-reference, a fabricated citation, a quantifier false for one member of its set) spanning the lens categories, run the panel, and measure per-hat and pooled recovery against the planted set. Because the ground truth is known by construction rather than sampled from what a human happened to notice, this is the only mechanism that yields a genuine, refreshable recall estimate rather than a frozen 2026-08-17 snapshot bounded by one human's attention on that day.
